A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Community Notes study, with matching research questions, corpus and principal analyses. The complete texts, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original analyses of 664K Community Notes, including source distributions, community ratings, manual annotations and an 8K-pair analysis of broader narratives and conspiracies.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical analyses and additionally reports 90% topic-classification accuracy and observations about classification errors.

M1.justification: The five-stage URL-classification pipeline, ModernBERT topic classifier and GPT-4o narrative-classification procedure remain unchanged. Both versions retain identical prompts in Listings 1 and 2; the added explanations do not establish a revised computational method.

E1.justification: Both versions analyze the same English-language Twitter/X corpus from January 2021 to January 2025 and retain the same source, topic, helpfulness and narrative-analysis tasks. Discussions of other platforms and collaborative fact-checking do not add evaluated datasets or scenarios.

E2.justification: The empirical comparisons retain the same groups, including notes with and without fact-checking sources and different helpfulness statuses. Newly cited studies, such as Maldita (2025), are discussed as related work rather than evaluated as additional comparators.

E3.justification: The stated filtering, sample sizes, models and validation procedures match. However, v1 Figure 10 shows one broader-narrative field, whereas v2 Figure 8 separately displays broader-narrative and conspiracy fields; the written 12-attribute guidelines remain unchanged. The PDFs do not resolve whether the annotation protocol changed or its documentation was corrected.

E4.justification: V2 Section 4.2 adds a topic-classification error analysis: references to AI-generated images can incorrectly trigger the technology label. Footnote 9 also newly reports similar trends when broader narratives and conspiracy theories are analyzed separately, although no separate numerical breakdown is provided.

E5.justification: Both versions report two authors independently labeling 100 balanced pairs, agreement of 0.88 and disagreement resolution through discussion. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: V1 describes topic-classification validation only as satisfactory; v2 reports 90% correct classifications and adds qualitative error and separate-category findings. The principal results remain unchanged, including the 5%/7%/1% fact-checking-source figures, narrative-classification F1 of 0.85 and the 22%/11%/28%/39% contingency table.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results, proofs or mathematical derivations. The added explanation of broader narratives clarifies an empirical annotation category rather than introducing a mathematical definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same research questions and central claims about professional fact-checking supporting Community Notes, particularly for broader narratives and conspiracies. V2's abstract emphasizes their interdependence, which v1 already states in its conclusion.

C2.justification: The expanded Broader Impact section proposes using notes to identify checkworthy claims, experts to resolve disputed notes and human-in-the-loop automation to assist both groups. It also calls professional fact-checking the only viable approach for partisan issues. The existing limitations concerning English-only coverage, missing context and limited manual annotation remain.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly notes that a note can contain multiple URLs and explains aggregation of narrative and conspiracy labels. Its replacement annotation screenshot supplies separate label columns and more descriptive headings. Model versions, access links, lookup tables, prompts and written annotation guidelines are retained; these documentation changes do not establish that the underlying study was rerun.

R1.justification: V2 identifies Maldita (2025) as closely related work and distinguishes its own finer-grained analysis. The expanded background adds research on professional versus community fact-checking, including Saeed et al. (2022) and Zhao and Naaman (2023), while the new recommendations cite Augenstein et al. (2025). The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the main-text/appendix structure: v1 Sections 2.1.2 and 2.2 become an Extended Background appendix, and Additional Material and Reproducibility become Appendices B and C. The example table moves out of the main narrative, background prose is revised, and the Broader Impact discussion is expanded.

P2.justification: V2 merges v1 Figures 2, 7 and 8 into a three-panel Figure 2 with consistent category ordering. Figure 5 reorders topics, harmonizes colors and corrects the vertical-axis label from Topic to Percentage without changing the distributions. The example table moves to the appendix, other displays are repositioned, and the annotation screenshot is replaced.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves transparency, research context and readability through quantified topic validation, a concrete error analysis, acknowledgment of closely related work and clearer figures. The main empirical evidence is unchanged. Gains remain limited by the unspecified topic-validation sample size, ambiguous annotation-protocol documentation and stronger policy assertions that receive no additional comparative evidence.
